evidence: image, column 1–2: '…管子量其重丨其丨民得其十君得其三則民疾作而為上虜矣'; the OCR has it correctly. The English says 'If the ruler takes … seven parts while the people keep only three'. The page says the people get ten and the ruler three, and there is no 'seven'. The numbers are invented and the beneficiary is reversed.

image, right-hand main column: subcolumn A '乃出私錢作氷磑丨其丨以濟饑' and subcolumn B '瘵構舍數十百楹居之全活甚衆' (both end the Wang Fangyi entry), then headword 年贏, then the small text '唐書崔從傳為淮南節度 / 副大使知節度事揚州凡'. The OCR orders this as 濟饑 / 年羸 / 唐書崔從傳… / 副大使…揚州凡 / 瘵構舍…, so the end of Wang Fangyi's sentence lands inside the Cui Cong entry, and 揚州凡 is cut off from 交易貲産…. One correction: the headword is not lost from the OCR. It is there as 年羸, with 羸 misread for 贏, the same misreading made for every headword on the page. The headword does vanish from the translation.

The English opens the Cui Cong entry with 'Yangzhou had <unclear>20 characters</unclear> and constructed hundreds of buildings to house people, saving many lives'. On the image, 構舍數十百楹居之全活甚衆 belongs to Wang Fangyi (previous page / column 1), and nothing on the leaf is illegible, so the 20-character gap is invented. '從皆蠲除之' is moved to the end of the Su Ting paragraph, and '又買麴丨其丨以佐用度' is dropped. The headword 年贏 is missing: both biographies sit under 分羸. A reader would credit Cui Cong with Wang Fangyi's famine housing.

image p.48: 'And bring thy sacred altar; tell ME where / That as a Husband thou didst once appear? / Bring ME the priest that ever join'd thy hand:'. OCR: 'That as a Priest that ever join'd thy hand:'. The error is real and serious: a line is lost and the two lines are spliced into nonsense. But this is an eye-skip omission splicing two lines (the first half of one, the second half of the next), not freely invented text.

image p.48: 'So, if his Back be Brass, he can appear, / And made of Iron that he doth not fear / For to contend so boldly with his God: / He now shall find…'. OCR: 'So, if his Back be Brass, he can appear, / For from Iron to Iron my word he'll bear. / He now shall find…'. The OCR line appears nowhere on the page and replaces two real lines.

image p.48 has 'As in the fifteenth page it doth appear;' (after 'Challenge is by Satan given'), 'For he shall know that I have seal'd his doom;' and 'For there I tell him, his proud waves are stay'd.'. All three are absent from the OCR, which goes straight from 'Power's there;' to 'And now his matchless power'. A fourth line, 'And all these Crosses shall on him appear;', is also missing.

image p.49 has 'And then their power they'll begin to see,' (after 'coming stroke:'), 'As in the seventeenth page it doth appear,' (after 'let them all enjoy.') and 'But to attempt it now, I say they dare—' (after 'all my subjects gain;'). All three are missing from the OCR.

The English pane copies the OCR line for line: 'That as a Priest that ever join'd thy hand:' and 'For from Iron to Iron my word he'll bear.' are both present, and the dropped lines are absent. The reader sees every OCR error. This is the same root error as claims 40-0 to 40-3, not an independent one.
The first text line of the image reads 'ΧΡΕ Τίς δῆτ' ἰατρὸς ἐστὶ νῦν ἐν τῇ πόλει' (Plut. 406). The OCR has 'ΧΡ Τί δαὶ; τί αὖ σὺ δῆτ’ ἐφ’ ἡμῶν ἐνθάδε;', which shares nothing with the leaf except δῆτ'.

image line 2: 'οὔτε γὰρ ὁ μισθὸς οὐδέν ἐστ' οὔθ' ἡ τέχνη' (written ουτεγαρ ὁ μιαθος ουδεν εστ' ουθ' η τεχνη). OCR: 'οὐ γὰρ ὁ μαθὸς δουλεύει τῇ τέχνῃ'. The OCR keeps γὰρ ὁ μ.θος … τέχνη from the leaf, so the line is misread into a fluent different sentence, not invented. The meaning changes from 'there is neither fee nor skill' to 'the reward does not serve the art', which is serious. The added speaker βλε has no red label on the leaf, but Plut. 407 is Blepsidemus's line, so that part is minor.

image: red 'Βλε', then 'πολὺ μὲν οὖν μὴ τοῖς θεοῖς(?)· μὴ νῦν διάτριβε'. OCR: 'βλέπω δὲ μὲν οὖν μὴ τοῖς θεοῖσι μηνίον λάτρειβε'. Much of the leaf survives (μὲν οὖν μὴ τοῖς θεοῖσ…), but πολὺ becomes βλέπω δὲ (the speaker label absorbed) and μὴ νῦν διάτριβε becomes μηνίον λάτρειβε. That is a misread, not an invention. It is serious because the English renders it 'do not serve the gods in anger' in place of 'don't delay'. The reviewer's quoted 'ὦ πρὸς θεῶν' may come from the vulgate rather than this manuscript.
The English 'What then? Why are you here with us again?' translates the OCR's invented first line. The leaf asks 'So what doctor is there now in the city?'.

English: 'For the reward does not serve the art.', followed by a note interpreting Blepsidemus's cynicism about profit. The note is commentary built on a misread line; the leaf says neither fee nor skill exists. One qualification: the underlying line is misread (O6, see 29-1), not wholly invented. The invented note is real either way.
image: red ΠΕ, then 'οἴεσθε δ' εἶναι τίνα με·' (Plut. 437, 'who do you think I am?'). The ink after εἶναι reads τινα με, not ὑμᾶς. OCR: 'ΠΕ οἴεσθε δ’ εἶναι ὑμᾶς.'

The English 'Who do you think you are?' follows the misread ὑμᾶς. The very next line, Chremylus's answer 'An innkeeper or an oil-flask seller!', describes Penia, so the exchange as stored no longer makes sense.

The image matches the OCR word for word: '…in hac secunda mora processere … ad unum omnes in tertia damnarentur mora … Adde, quòd non unius … tantùm criminis rei … à minoribus ad maiora & atrociora …', ending with 'fune-'. The English starts with 'ral fall, they were cast down', completing the catchword, and continues with about 150 words on grace, darkness and pride. None of it maps to any Latin sentence on the page: the second and third mora, the plurality of crimes, and the minor-to-major progression are all absent. This is arguably T5, a lookahead that translates a guessed continuation beyond the catchword, but it is serious under either label.

image, column 2–3: '其所得以為性者皆天地之志為氣之帥者也然體有偏正之殊'. The OCR has it correctly. The English goes from 'the energy of heaven and earth that fills the space between them' straight to 'Because what they obtain is different…'. The 性/帥 sentence is dropped, and 然體有偏正之殊 is also flattened into 'what they obtain is different'. The commentary's pairing of body as qi (塞) and nature as the will that commands qi (帥) is lost.

image, last paragraph: 'Ասէ Յոհան. Փուշ և տատասկ բուսցի: Ասէ այրն. Ի մարմինդ քո բուսցի փուշ և տատասկ, փոխանակ զի տարապարտուց անիծանես զմեզ:'. OCR: 'Ասէ Յոհան. Փուշ և տատասկ բուսցի, փոխանակ զի տարապարտուց անիծանես զմեզ:'. The OCR skips from the first բուսցի to the second, so the man's counter-curse is lost.

English: 'Yohan said, "May thorns and thistles grow, because you curse us with your indebtedness."'. The serious harm is the OCR's O5 omission carried into the English: the counter-curse is given to the bishop, and the next line's punishment no longer follows. That is an inherited omission, not a misread (O6). Separately, տարապարտուց ('unjustly, in vain') is mistranslated as 'with your indebtedness', a lexical error that adds to the damage.
